name: Gletscherweg Kaunertal
kurzbeschreibung: The high-alpine Kaunertal Glacier Trail starts at the Gepatschhaus, exploring the glacial forefield of the Gepatschferner.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Gletscherweg Kaunertal at the head of the Kaunertal valley is one of Austria's most awe-inspiring and educational high-alpine educational hiking routes. Beginning at the historic Gepatschhaus refuge at an altitude of 1,928 meters, the carefully marked thematic trail leads through the vast glacial forefield of the Gepatschferner – the second-largest contiguous glacier in the Republic of Austria, situated in the Ötztal Alps. Along the route, hikers witness first-hand how advancing and retreating ice has sculpted the landscape across millennia. Colossal lateral moraines, polished bedrock slabs, roaring glacial meltwater torrents, and resilient pioneer plants reclaiming bare stone make the trail a living open-air laboratory of earth and climate history. Interpretive displays by the Kaunergrat Nature Park provide deep insights into glaciology.

Route & Requirements

The classic glacier hike begins right at the storied Gepatschhaus or at the toll station of the Kaunertal Glacier Road. The trek covers roughly six kilometers with 350 meters of elevation change, taking approximately 2.5 to 3 hours of active walking time. The route follows narrow alpine tracks, boulder fields, and glacially smoothed granite slabs, requiring ankle-high hiking boots with grippy profile soles, weatherproof mountain apparel, and solid physical fitness. Surefootedness is essential when traversing rocky terrain and cross-secured footbridges spanning glacial streams. The trail is completely unsuitable for strollers; however, surefooted older children will find the primeval landscape an unforgettable adventure ground. Sufficient drinking water, snacks, and sun protection are mandatory.

Visit & Arrival

The Kaunertal Glacier Trail is safely accessible during the snow-free summer months from mid-June to early October; access to the educational trail is free of charge. Arrive by car via the A12 Inntal motorway and B180 to Prutz, continue along the Kaunertaler Landesstraße to Feichten, and ascend the toll-road Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße to the Gepatschhaus (parking on site). From late June to September, regional Postbuses connect Landeck and Feichten directly with the Gepatschhaus and the upper glacier restaurant.

Tips

Observe the raw kinetic power of glacial meltwater at the Fernergrieß torrents and keep an eye out for small quartz crystals in the moraine gravel. After the hike, visit the heritage-listed Gepatschhaus, Austria's oldest Alpine Club refuge, to enjoy hearty alpine cooking in its historical pine wood parlour.
preis: Theme trail free of charge; Kaunertal Glacier Road subject to toll
oeffnungszeiten: Safe to hike from mid-June to early October (weather dependent)
